question: Is streaming DORMANT (a wide hot-expert working set re-enters disk-I/O-bound decode here) or DEAD (compute/RAM binds even under wide routing)?
method: same box+model, warm, greedy. Force wide expert coverage via a high-entropy ~2673-token multi-domain prompt (near-full 128-expert/layer coverage). CONTROL for the context-length confound: an equal-length (~2700-token) LOW-ENTROPY prompt (identical repeated token -> narrow routing, same attention/KV compute). Isolates routing-width I/O from context-length attention compute.

attribution.context_length_attention_compute: 9.2 -> 3.9 tok/s : DOMINANT drop, from long-context attention (same in both long runs, present with NARROW routing) -> not expert I/O.
attribution.routing_width_expert_io: 3.9 -> 2.9 tok/s : the isolated wide-routing penalty at equal context length = ~26% slower, ~1.8x per-token disk (75 vs 41 MB/token, +~34 MB/token attributable to expert faulting).
attribution.disk_saturation: NEVER reached the 1.02 GB/s scatter ceiling in any regime; random-fault reads top ~400-490 MB/s. Decode is not cleanly disk-pegged even under max-entropy wide routing.

verdict_detail: Widening the active set DOES re-introduce real per-token expert-fault I/O (+~34 MB/token, ~1.8x), so streaming is NOT dead -- it is dormant. BUT the effect is SECONDARY: the dominant long-context binder is compute (attention) + RAM-bandwidth, the wide-routing I/O penalty is only ~26%, and the drive is never saturated. On this box+model, streaming's payoff would be marginal. Its real home is Fork-1 RELOCATION (a larger MoE whose active set >> RAM and where expert-fault I/O dominates attention, or a higher-bandwidth/compute tier), not this model here.

confirms_refines.m4_direction: CONFIRMED across narrow AND wide workloads -- disk never saturates; expert I/O is present but not the primary binder here.
confirms_refines.m4_number: overturned (per probe-verdict.json): warm narrow ~9.2, workload-dependent 2.9-14 range; 4.3 was a cold per-invocation artifact.
confirms_refines.streaming_scope: not 'dead', but 'dormant + weak on this box+model'; the streaming thesis targets a bigger-MoE / different-hardware regime (Fork 1).

caveats: 48-token gen windows are short -> tok/s noisy; the equal-length control is what makes the width attribution robust (not the absolute 2.9/3.9).

scatter ceiling 1.02 GB/s is M3's contiguous-read figure; random expert faults achieve less (~400-490 MB/s observed), so 'not saturated at 1.02' understates how close random-fault I/O is to ITS own ceiling -- the width penalty is real even though sub-1GB/s.
bigger-MoE test (active set >> RAM) needs a model download -> deliberately NOT run here; it is the natural Fork-1 relocation probe.
